[b]The Chamber of the Peoples & The Offices of Consantin VII:  March 5th, 2025[/b]

A low murmur filled the Chamber of the Peoples as the nation's 43 representatives filed into their seats, a few worried looks were cast here and there as a thick tension hung over the air. Any day would be tense, however today was expected to be far more explosive than any other day in the legislative history of North Thýven. Amongst these legislators, elected by the people to represent their interests, but not oft filled with their own interests, was Consantin VII.

Consantin VII was a controversial figure among the legislators, his rise to political office was fraught with suspicions and accusations of vile nepotism, however, the son of the President rejected these accusations against his character and pretended not to hear them most often.

He was a tall fellow, his dark brown hair sweeping low close to his hazel eyes which seemed to pierce into the soul of whomever he was talking to. Moving through the hall he found his seat, a worn desk next to the opposition leader of the Reform Party Jænus Albringer, a vivacious and charismatic woman with a reputation for deviancy unbecoming of a lady.

As the final members filed into their seats, the Prelate of the Chamber of the Peoples arrived with little fanfare, carrying a thick book that nearly dwarfed his short stature, he made his way to the podium.

Greetings fellow members of this esteemed chamber, he huffed as he finally reached the podium and set the book down with a thud.

Greetings! Replied those assembled in solemn unison, this was all procedure to them.

Today we gather here my dear brothers and sisters to discuss the challenge with which the Senate put forth against the president, seemingly ignoring the will of the people and seeking to subvert our country and constitution, stated the prelate.

Consantin VII listened for a few moments before tuning out the prelates droning on about procedures and vote plans. Casting his eyes upwards to the guest boxes on the second level of the hall he noted the presence of various shrouded females and  males, priests and women of the Adní. He shuddered slightly as he stared at them, a constant reminder of his mothers eye over him.

He was stirred from his thoughts by the prelate declaring that the floor had opened to debate, a long and tedious process where various members of various parties threw out insults and hurled objections at each other. 

The first to rise to speak was Ergard Dollins, a representative from a small region in the south of the country, The constitution, my dear friends, he stated, Is secure in the operations of the senate, if the senate voted the way it did, then there can be no objection, he continued with a dramatic sweep of his hand, voices murmured from the more anti-presidential individuals in the room.

Yet, began a voice, of which Consantin identified as that of representative Severen, a youthful acquaintance of his, Members of the senate laid accusations against the speaker before us, and precedent states that if the senate should lay a motion before the chamber, then the chamber should move to consider it, stated Severen, more murmurs filled the room.

Is it enough though that there is no evidence for these accusations by those members of the senate? stated another representative of whom Consantin did not recognise.

Hear, hear, cried another. 

Consantin finally rose and began to speak, hoping a more measured response by the chamber could be pushed forward, My dear friends, he began, The senate vote was clearly a tie, of which was broken by the speaker as confirmed by one of the protesting senators himself, now of course this doesnt warrant that we ignore any investigation, but, I should ask, are we looking at the right person? he stated, a few more murmurs filled the room. 

AH, of course the young Consantin would fill this room, with words of such sweet renown, yet we forget even now, that he is the son of the despot we seek to remove? stated Jænus Albringer rising swiftly to counter his talk, a louder murmur.

Hold your tongue and set it down, for what means of accusation is this, was not Consantin chosen forth by the citizens' voice? stated Severen.

By what means indeed, and you, you his ally, you question me? replied  Jænus Albringer half mockingly.

Halt, halt, this talk is not appropriate, back to order or I shall see the three of you brought to knee, stated the prelate banging his gavel. 

Now it is clear to me that this matter is set, I shall permit a temporary recess for discussion to be held between the parties, then shall we properly vote? enquired the Prelate, looking around for any sign of dissent, and seeing none he would continue, Then let it be affirmed that a recess shall be called, two hours and then, we shall vote, he stated before descending the podium. 

Consantin sighed slightly as he rose from his seat giving Jænus a polite and cordial nod as she made her way past him to discuss whatever she was to discuss with her fellow partymates. Consantin wasnt one to hang around and chitter chatter, he knew the position of his party quite well and preferred to have meetings in his chambers, out of the ears of the media and other parties.

Moving quickly out of the grand hall he made his way through the marbled corridors of the Peoples Basilica, passing by portraits and statues and other grand decorations which gave off an air of bright nationalism and pretentious optimism. Consantin had moved and walked through these halls many times, tourists, visitors, and government officials bustling here and there and to and fro, yet today the halls were surprisingly hushed, the tension in the chamber had seemingly spread throughout the building. 

As he  neared his office in the west wing of the basilica, he heard a voice ring out along the corridor, Consantin! cried the voice. Consantin stopped and turned to face the voice to see a bright eyed Severen walking quickly toward him. 

Ah, Lucius Severen! declared Consantin moving to greet his friend and closest ally in the chamber, I assume this is about that meeting you wanted to have earlier, no? enquired Consantin, referring to a conversation the two had earlier in the morning. 

Oh yes, I forgot about that, if you are available, I am available now, replied Severen, brushing the long ginger locks of his hair out of his face. 

Come now my friend, let us meet, I am sure you and I have much to discuss, replied Consantin moving towards his office.

Consantins office was richly decorated, portraits of family members hung on the oak panelled walls, and a cozy atmosphere seemed to permeate the place, his office consisted of three rooms, a board room, a sitting room, and his office itself which was of a more utilitarian style and sparsely decorated save for a bookcase and the grand oak desk which sat at the center of the office, a gift from his father. It was here that Consantin and Severen moved to meet.

Now Severen, what is it that you wished to meet with me for? enquired Consantin after finally seating himself.

Well, with the recent senate vote and concerns about the integrity of the senate, particularly in the leadership of the speaker, there is a concern in my party, that the security of the dynastic presidency might be endangered, replied Severen.

Consantin nodded, listening to Severen. Severen was a member and one of the top ranking officials in the Party for Justice, the nation's oldest and most centrist political parties, the PoJ had often sided with the presidency in most matters however, preferring stability over radical reform. 

What do you mean by security? enquired Consantin, his eyebrows creasing slightly with concern.

The strength of the presidency, with the pushback from the Chamber of the Peoples that seems to be mounting, the Senate might find itself embattled or even overthrown to a degree by the Chamber, and as you are fully aware, the Senate and the Supreme Court act as the primary protectors for the presidency and your fathers powers, replied Severen.

I see what you mean, replied Consantin, If one wall is taken down with this vote, then the chamber might go after the court, and then the presidency itself, he stated. 

Yes, correct, I mean the court already stands quite divided in its nature, and highly partisan, thankfully we have Justice Doma keeping order and unity therein, replied Severen. 

So what do you propose, Lucius? Enquired  Consantin, leaning forward slightly.

Well, right now the PoJ stands to vote for the investigation of the speaker of the senate, however, they might reconsider their vote if you are willing to join them in coalition to pass the 2025 budget bill that has been bouncing across the parties, replied Severen.

Consantin frowned, the bill had been in contention for his own party, the Presidential Party had wanted a more slimmed down version of the bill which had become highly bloated with extra additions in such places as infrastructure and other such expenditures. 

Id have to hold a meeting to see what the others think of it, your offer is intriguing, however, you fully know my position on the bill, replied Consantin hesitantly.

Of course, it is bloated, we need to remove the large spending for infrastructure and other such things and focus purely on government functions and such things in this bill, I am fully aware, replied Severen listing off Consantins reasons, But, if you want your father to remain secure in his position, you must make a compromise, and form a coalition, stated Severen. 

Consantin remained silent for a few moments as he thought; such a drastic move would most certainly drive the smaller parties to unite as well, however, if the Presidential Party and Party of Justice united they would unite over half the chamber. 

I shall consider it, however, can I have your assurance that you will vote against the motion yourself? enquired Consantin finally replying. 

As your friend, and not your political ally, I will do so, though my party might shun me for it, replied Severen.

Let them shun, if my father succeeds they will have no tongue with which to shun any longer, replied Consantin. 

Very well then, I expect an answer soon on my offer, replied Severen rising from his seat.

And an answer you shall have, replied Consantin also rising, moving to shake his friend's hand.

Let it be so, replied Severen shaking Consantins hand before moving out of the office.

[b]Name of Religion[/b]: Rahmaism 
[b]Date of Origin[/b]: 6th century CE 
[b]About[/b]: Rahmaism is a monotheistic religion that worships Al-Rahman, the all-compassionate God. It draws inspiration from diverse cultures around Shamat, emphasizing compassion, justice, and community. 
[b]Beliefs[/b]: Rahmaism centers on the belief in one God, Al-Rahman, with a line of prophets led by Musa the Wise. The Rahmanic Scrolls guide followers with teachings, parables, and poetry. Emphasis is placed on compassion, justice, daily prayers, communal worship, charity (Zakat), fasting during Rahmanan, and an annual pilgrimage to Rahmanabad. 
[b]Geographical Location[/b]: Rahmaism originated in the western part of The Shamats, specifically in the region of modern-day Wendana, and has since spread across the continent.
